newsitem.title: USA: NHL-ROY RECORDS SECOND SHUTOUT IN FOUR DAYS FOR AVALANCHE.
newsitem.headline: NHL-ROY RECORDS SECOND SHUTOUT IN FOUR DAYS FOR AVALANCHE.

text.p: Patrick Roy recorded his second shutout in four days and the 32nd of his career as the defending Stanley Cup champion Colorado Avalanche blanked the Chicago Blackhawks 2-0 on Friday.
Roy rebounded from a miserable performance on Thursday in which he surrendered four goals over the final 10 minutes in a 6-6 tie with Anaheim, by turning back all 34 Chicago shots on goal.
"After the last game, I was pretty upset with myself. I was lazy and I didn't work hard," said Roy, who backstopped Colorado to the team's first NHL title in June.
"Tonight, I was more aggressive and more sharp. It was important for me to play good tonight because the last game the guys played good and I let them down."
Roy came up with his best saves in the second period, denying Kevin Miller on a 2-on-none break and stopping Denis Savard's wrist shot at the end of a 2-on-1.

Rookie defenceman Aaron Miller opened the scoring with 4:11 left in the second period when he took a pass from Stephane Yelle and deposited the puck just under the Chicago crossbar for his first NHL goal.
"I'm sure it's one he'll remember for a long time," Colorado coach Marc Crawford said. "He played a super game."
Scott Young made it 2-0 with a powerplay tally at 4:31 of the third. He took a cross-ice pass from Sandis Ozolinsh at the left faceoff circle and put a low wrister past Ed Belfour.
Belfour made 26 stops for the Blackhawks, who have been shut out in their last two games.
"Tonight, our guys played like pros," said Crawford. "It was a team effort."
In Ottawa, Alexandre Daigle and Alexei Yashin scored third-period goals as the Senators broke a 16-game winless streak against the Pittsburgh Penguins with a 3-2 victory.

Daigle tied the game with 15:41 remaining when he put a rebound of Randy Cunneyworth's shot past goaltender Ken Wregget. Yashin scored a powerplay goal just over three minutes later when his shot tipped Wregget's glove and went over the goalie's head and down his back into the net.
In the last 16 meetings between the two clubs, the Senators had lost 15 and tied once.
Pittsburgh's dynamic duo of Jaromir Jagr and Mario Lemieux scored in the first period for the 0-3 Penguins.
But Ottawa goalie Damian Rhodes shut down the Pens after Lemieux's goal at 10:51, making 27 saves, including 14 in the third period.
In Detroit, Robert Reichel's goal early in the second period lifted the Calgary Flames to a 2-1 victory over the Red Wings.
Reichel took a feed from rookie defenceman Chris O'Sullivan and blasted a slap shot from just inside the blue line that deflected off Chris Osgood's blocker into the net.
Detroit grabbed a 1-0 lead at 7:31 of the first period when Doug Brown picked up a rebound and lifted the puck over goaltender Trevor Kidd.
But Calgary tied the game less than four minutes later when rookie Jarome Iginla redirected O'Sullivan's shot past Osgood for his third goal in four games.

At Washington, Peter Bondra had two goals and two assists and Phil Housley added a goal and two assists to lead the Capitals to their first win of the season, a 6-2 triumph over the Tampa Bay Lightning.

Bondra assisted on Jason Allison's powerplay goal in the first period and Michal Pivonka's tally in the second as the Caps built a 2-0 lead. He scored his first goal of the season midway through the third to extend the lead to 4-1, then closed the scoring with 3:33 remaining.
Washington goalie Jim Carey faced just three shots in the first period and made 21 saves in all.
In Edmonton, Brett Hull's first goal of the season snapped a third-period tie and Grant Fuhr made 26 saves as the St Louis Blues defeated the Oilers 3-1.

Hull, held without a point in the Blues' first three games, took a pass from Chris Pronger and streaked down the left side before flipping the puck high over Curtis Joseph with just over 12 minutes left.
Jim Campbell added an insurance goal with 1:11 left in the game. David Oliver got the lone Edmonton goal, beating Fuhr at 4:47 of the second period.
